_note: Copy to clients/<slug>-demo/client-inputs.json (the project folder, created before the project; the only copy) and fill every double-brace value in step 2; scripts/fill-client.cjs check refuses any value still in double braces. Leave the null fields null: scripts/measure-site.cjs --into <this file> fills loader, word, introKey and brand.mark (the .png twin of the loader's image) in step 4, new-project.sh fills logoWidth in step 5, and measure-site.cjs --storyboard … --into fills SERVICE_FOCUS and zoomCopy in step 6. Copy every fact character for character from where the site prints it (the visit card or the footer). examples/discount-used-cars/client-inputs.json is a filled copy.
domain: {{public host without www, from business.siteUrl, owner-confirmed}}
_partBDomain: Stays null until the owner confirms the desk host may be shown in the URL pill.
_partB: Leave null for a site with no desk. With the desk (the deliverable is then part A + part B, about 80 s), fill it in three stages, each checked by fill-client.cjs check --stage <stage>: desk (runbook B0, before any desk capture): { "onboarding": "owner-fees" | "sales" — the USER's answer to 'Film the owner's first sign-in including Your Fees (I type a fee figure you give me), or film a salesperson's first sign-in (no fees screen)?', never chosen for them; "demoFee": { "cents": 15000, "source": "owner" | "user-approved", "note": "who gave it, when" } on the owner-fees path only (named as a demo input in the README and the send note, never on screen) }; post (runbook B5, measured on the captures): "cuts": { "signinPainted": n, "saleSkeleton": [a, b], "readbackRelease": [a, b] } (scripts/measure-desk-cuts.cjs --into), "docFileName": the 130-U's downloaded name, e.g. 130-U_Carter_812345.pdf.
_deskClock: With a desk: the capture day at 14:00 in the dealer's zone with that day's offset, e.g. 2026-10-02T14:00:00-05:00. It is the date the desk server stamps on the documents (its real date), so the pad's 'Signed:' matches the paper. Never the site's clock (fill-client refuses the fallback).
_demo: With a desk: { "phone": "<area code>5550142" (a fictional 555 number in the dealer's area code), "addressPartB": { "street", "city", "zip", "county", "checkedOn", "how" } — a street NUMBER that does not exist on a real street, typed into the read-back (lesson B13: search it before capture), "addressNarrated": { same keys } — narrated cut only: a block number on a commercial road the Census geocoder resolves (the autofill line needs it) and no listed home (lesson N2): curl 'https://geocoding.geo.census.gov/geocoder/locations/onelineaddress?address=<street, city, TX zip>&benchmark=Public_AR_Current&format=json' must return a match; record the URL and the date in how / checkedOn. No web access: ask the user for an address }. The demo people (Maria Lopez, James Carter, licence 41927365) and the preview lot's car are house values.
_voice: Leave null: the house voice is Kokoro af_heart at speed 0.95. Only a client decision changes it: { "voice": "af_bella", "speed": 0.95, "why": "the owner chose it from samples on <date>" }; voice.py refuses any other voice without this.
_deskUrl: Only used as VITE_DESK_URL for the capture build, so the drawer's Admin row renders. It is never navigated in part A. If the client has no sale desk, stop and ask the user: the house cut ends on that row.
facts: {{street, city as the site prints it}}
{{short hours exactly as the visit card prints them, no closed days}}
_facts: Only business.ts fields sourced OWNER or TXDMV, in this order: web address (www. + domain), phone as (000) 000-0000, street and city, short hours. No prices, no claims.
_outroLines: Exactly facts[0]; facts[1] + ' · ' + facts[2]; facts[3]. fill-client.cjs check enforces it.

brand.logoReverse: clients/{{client-slug}}-site/public/brand/{{the full-colour logo the site shows on its black bands or footer}}

_brand: mark is filled by measure-site.cjs --into (the .png of the loader's image). logoReverse is the logo the site itself shows on dark (footer or black bands); if the site has none, ask the user. Never recolour or invert a logo for the film.
clock: {{2026-09-30T14:00:00 plus the dealer's UTC offset that day, e.g. -05:00 for Central daylight time}}
_clock: Wednesday 2026-09-30 at 14:00 in the dealer's time zone. If the dealer is closed on Wednesdays, the next open weekday at 14:00. measure-site.cjs checks that the site shows 'Open now' then.
_stingMarkWidth: Leave null: it becomes loader.mark width × 600/360, so the sting is the loader drawn 1.667× larger for every client and the hand-off shrink (to ~0.62) is the same move as Discount's.
_logoWidth: theme.outro.logoWidth. Leave null: new-project.sh sets min(760, round(300 × logo width / height)) from logoReverse (Discount's 2.6:1 logo gives 760, a 1.28:1 logo 384) and prints it. Set a number only to override, with the reason in the README.

storyboard.FINDER_QUERY: {{a model in stock, about 5 characters, e.g. F-150}}
storyboard.SERVICE_TILE: {{label of the middle service-band tile, exactly as the site prints it}}
storyboard._storyboard: Defaults are the house values (Discount's). BODY: Truck if the dealer has trucks in stock, else SUV if it has SUVs, else Truck. SERVICE_FOCUS is always measured (measure-site.cjs --storyboard … --rects); the others are checked by the same run. See references/storyboard.md, 'Adapting the house storyboard'.

_overrides: Timing changes the page forces (e.g. a longer FINDER_QUERY), applied after filling: [{ "shot": "2-scroll", "path": "actions.8.perCharSec", "value": 0.12, "why": "…" }]. path is dot-separated into the filled shot (array indexes as in the template). Every override is listed in the README; each one needs a reason and a full re-verify.
_narration: Leave null for the house films. For the narrated long cut only: scripts/fill-narration.cjs init <this file> writes the block to fill (the house script's variables: what is said, what is shown, the flags for the optional lines, and checked: the features walked on this client's desk). The variables table and the fact-check are in assets/narration/script-template.md; examples/discount-used-cars/client-inputs.json has a filled one. fill-narration.cjs lines / script then write narration/lines.json and narration/script.md.
_zoomCopy: Leave null: measure-site.cjs --storyboard … --into writes the text each zoom shows (step 6); the README lists it for the owner.
